scope: Gap-focused emulator discovery beyond the existing 178 emulator records: mainframe, TI-99/4A, Acorn Archimedes/Risc PC, SHARP X68000, RCA COSMAC, and Android-hosted PC-98/DOS systems. Each record is a distinct emulator implementation or maintained emulator application, not a general frontend or compatibility layer.

projects.title: Hercules System/370, ESA/390, and z/Architecture Emulator
projects.game: IBM System/370, ESA/390, and z/Architecture operating systems and applications
projects.platform: IBM System/370, ESA/390, and 64-bit z/Architecture mainframes
projects.status: The production-quality 3.xx Spinhawk branch remains maintained; the latest upstream commit checked was 2026-07-16. The separate Hyperion development repository has substantially older source activity, so this entry points to the 3.xx release stream.
projects.summary: Hercules is an open-source software implementation of IBM System/370, ESA/390, and 64-bit z/Architecture mainframe systems. It models a mainframe CPU and channel-attached devices so compatible operating systems and software can run on a modern host.
projects.strategy: Full system emulation of IBM mainframe architectures and emulated I/O devices.
projects.source_available: Public C source repository; the official project site identifies the Q Public Licence (QPL).

projects.title: Classic99
projects.status: Maintained; the public repository received an upstream commit on 2026-10-12. The project README describes the package as open source under restrictive terms and includes TI-licensed ROMs; users should review the manual before redistributing it.
projects.summary: Windows emulator for the Texas Instruments TI-99/4A home computer. It provides cartridge and disk support, a debugger, and TI ROM images under separately stated license restrictions.
projects.strategy: Software emulation of TI-99/4A computer hardware and peripherals.
projects.source_available: Public source repository; maintainer describes its license as restrictive, and bundled TI firmware has separate terms.

projects.title: Swift 99/a
projects.platform: Texas Instruments TI-99/4A home computer; macOS 12 or later
projects.status: A working macOS emulator according to its maintainer, but still an early project with some documented unimplemented hardware and no tagged GitHub release. The latest source push checked was 2026-05-09.
projects.summary: Native TI-99/4A emulator written from scratch for macOS. The README documents TMS9900 CPU, TMS9918A video, PSG audio, optional speech synthesis, disk and cartridge support, and outstanding gaps such as cassette input and some cartridge banking schemes.
projects.strategy: Hardware-level emulation of the TI-99/4A CPU, video, sound, I/O, and memory system.
projects.source_available: Public source repository under BSD-2-Clause; bundled TI ROM data is separately identified in project documentation.

projects.title: RPCEmu Extended
projects.platform: Acorn Risc PC and A7000 families, including experimental A7000+ and Phoebe configurations; Windows, macOS, and Linux hosts
projects.status: Active; v2.0.0 was released on 2026-09-07 and the repository shows commits through 2026-10-04. The project documents release builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux, with experimental machine configurations called out separately.
projects.summary: GPL-2.0 fork of RPCEmu for Acorn Risc PC and A7000 computers. It emulates multiple ARM processor cards and RISC OS configurations and adds a dynamic recompiler, save/resume, expansion devices, networking, debugger, and package-management tools.
projects.strategy: Full machine emulation for Acorn Risc PC/A7000 hardware, including ARM CPUs, memory, video, storage, expansion devices, and peripherals.

projects.title: Arculator
projects.game: Acorn Archimedes computer software and games
projects.platform: Acorn Archimedes A3xx, A4xx, A3000, A540, A5000, A30x0, and A4000 configurations
projects.status: Legacy/dormant project: the public source tree describes Arculator 0.99, with no newer release found and the latest repository commit checked dated 2015-01-18. The original author-hosted page describes the Windows build; system ROMs must be supplied separately.
projects.summary: C-based emulator for Acorn Archimedes computers using ARM2, ARM250, or ARM3 configurations, with 512 KB to 16 MB RAM, floppy drives, IDE hard disks, and multiple RISC OS/Arthur ROM configurations. Its public source tree does not declare a license.
projects.strategy: Software emulation of Archimedes computer hardware and peripherals.
projects.source_available: Public C source repository; no project license declaration was found in the checked tree.

projects.title: PX68K Libretro Core
projects.game: SHARP X68000 computer software and games
projects.status: Community-maintained Libretro fork; the latest repository push checked was 2026-08-22. No tagged release was listed. The README requires users to supply X68000 BIOS files and supported disk-image content.
projects.summary: GPL-2.0 Libretro core for emulating SHARP X68000 computers, based on the hissorii px68k project with a C68K CPU-core backport for x64 support. It accepts X68000 disk and hard-disk formats through Libretro frontends.
projects.strategy: Full X68000 system emulation exposed through the Libretro core interface.

projects.title: MPX68K
projects.game: SHARP X68000 computer software and games
projects.platform: SHARP X68000 → macOS 12 or later (Intel and Apple Silicon)
projects.status: Active; the repository received an upstream commit on 2026-10-12 and its README documents version 4.2 and builds for Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.
projects.summary: Native macOS X68000 emulator with a SwiftUI/SpriteKit front end and px68k-derived C/C++ emulation components. It supports floppy and hard disk images, adjustable CPU clocks, controller input, display rotation, and optional MIDI output; users provide ROMs.
projects.strategy: X68000 machine emulation using the px68k core and C68K CPU emulator, integrated with a native macOS application.
projects.source_available: Public source repository; bundled components retain distinct license and attribution terms documented by the maintainer.

projects.title: WebX68k
projects.game: SHARP X68000 computer software and games
projects.platform: SHARP X68000; modern multi-threaded WebAssembly-capable browsers
projects.status: Active; the public repository received a commit on 2026-09-28. The project provides a live browser build and documents Firefox, Chromium-based browsers, and Safari considerations for its WebAssembly threading and storage features.
projects.summary: Browser-based X68000 emulator player powered by a px68k Libretro core compiled to WebAssembly. It provides disk management, persistent browser storage, and a directly usable online machine; its JavaScript/TypeScript interface is part of a wider C/WASM emulator stack.
projects.strategy: X68000 hardware emulation through px68k-libretro compiled to WebAssembly, with a browser frontend.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-2.0 source repository; the px68k-derived core and frontend license terms are documented upstream.

projects.title: RCA Studio II and Studio III Emulator
projects.game: RCA Studio II/III games and software for COSMAC VIP, FRED, and RCA arcade systems
projects.platform: RCA Studio II and Studio III; COSMAC VIP; RCA FRED and related CDP1802 systems
projects.status: Maintained personal preservation project; the repository received source updates through 2026-06-19. The author describes the application as a Processing-language port and extension of Paul Robson’s COSMAC/Studio II emulation code. No SPDX license is declared in the checked repository.
projects.summary: Processing application that emulates RCA Studio II/III systems and related CDP1802 machines, including COSMAC VIP/CHIP-8, RCA FRED, and RCA arcade hardware. It models CPU timing and system video/audio, and accepts program/cartridge image files supplied by the user.
projects.strategy: CDP1802 instruction and timing emulation with platform-specific video, audio, memory, and input devices.
projects.source_available: Public source repository; no project license declaration was found in the checked tree.

projects.title: Kairo98
projects.game: NEC PC-9801 / PC-98 games and software
projects.platform: NEC PC-9801 / PC-98; Android ARM64 devices running Android 8.0 or later
projects.status: Active; GitHub release v1.1.1 was published on 2026-10-15 (local date), and the repository was updated the same day. The Android app uses a pinned Neko Project 21/W emulator core and users supply any required BIOS, font, and sound ROMs.
projects.summary: Android PC-98 emulator app with a game library, per-game controls and settings, save states, on-screen keyboard, and disk-image management. It integrates a pinned Neko Project 21/W core with ymfm sound emulation; the project is GPL-2.0-or-later and is not an official release of those upstream cores.
projects.strategy: Android application integrating a pinned Neko Project 21/W PC-98 hardware-emulation core and ymfm audio core.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-2.0-or-later source repository; third-party emulator and audio components retain their own licenses.

projects.title: KairoDos
projects.game: DOS games and IBM PC-compatible software
projects.platform: IBM PC-compatible DOS systems; Android ARM64 devices running Android 8.0 or later
projects.status: Active; GitHub release v1.1.1 was published on 2026-10-15 (local date), and the source repository was updated the same day. It runs DOSBox Staging with ARM64 dynamic recompilation; KairoDos is an independent Android application, not an official DOSBox Staging release.
projects.summary: Android app for running DOS games and software, with a library, controller/touch mapping, on-screen keyboard, and per-game configuration. It integrates DOSBox Staging and exposes DOS prompt/setup workflows; users provide their own DOS software.
projects.strategy: DOSBox Staging PC hardware emulation adapted for Android ARM64, including dynamic recompilation for real/protected-mode CPU profiles.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-2.0-or-later first-party source; the bundled combination is distributed under GPLv3 terms due to third-party components.
